source_text:
εἰ δὲ τοῦτο ἀληθές ἐστιν, κατὰ τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς ἐρῶ· ἄρα οὐκ ἦν οὐδ' ἔσται ἐν βίῳ τὸ καλόν, οὔτε τίς ποτ' αὐτὸ ἐνήργησεν, εἴγε κατ' ἀναίρεσιν τοῦ καλοῦ καὶ ἀγαθοῦ ἐπὶ παντὸς ἀνθρώπου ἐκλαμβάνωσιν, ὅτι ὃ θέλω ἀγαθόν, τοῦτο οὐ ποιῶ, ἀλλ' ὃ μισῶ τοῦτο
πράσσω. πόθεν δὲ καὶ ἐν τῷ τῶν ἀνθρώπων βίῳ 5 ἀρετῶν ὀνόματα εὑρέθη; εἰ δέ εἰσιν ἐνεργοῦντες τὸ καλόν, κἂν ὀλίγοι εἶεν οἱ τοῦτο δρῶντες, ἄρ' οὐχ οἱ πάντες φήσουσιν· οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι οὐκ οἰκεῖ ἐν ἡμῖν ἀγαθόν· ὃ γὰρ ἠθέλησαν ἀγαθόν, τοῦτο πράττουσιν. εἰ δὲ οἱ τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐνεργοῦντες ἐν σαρκὶ ὑπάρχοντες τοῦτο ἐνεργοῦσιν, καὶ οἱ τοῦτο μὴ ποιοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ κακὸν ἐν σαρκί εἰσίν, ἄρ' οὐ τῇ σαρκὶ τὸ αἴτιον τοῦ μὴ γίνεσθαι τὸ ἀγαθὸν περιαπτέον, ἀλλὰ τῇ τούτων μαλακοψυχίᾳ. εἰ γὰρ τοῖς ἐθέλουσι τὸ καλὸν ποιῆσαι παροικεῖται τὸ κακόν, ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ τοῖς ἐθέλουσι κακοεργεῖν οὐ καλὸν παράκειται, προνοήσαντες δὲ καὶ προθελήσαντες ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον ἐνεργείας ἔρχονται, ἄρ' οὐ φύσει καὶ οὐσίᾳ τὰ σώματα ἡμῶν ἐστι φαῦλα· τῶν γὰρ πρακτέων ἡμῶν προηγεῖται βουλὴ καὶ θέλησις, ψυχῆς δὲ ταῦτα φρόνημα ἐχούσης αὐτεξούσιον, ῥέψαι δυναμένης πρὸς ἃς βούλεται πράξεις. Νυνὶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτό, ἀλλ' ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία. ἀπελογήσατο διὰ τούτου τοῦ λογίου, ὅτι περ οὐ φαύλη κατὰ φύσιν ἡ σάρξ· οὐ γὰρ ἡ σὰρξ ἣν περικείμεθα οἰκεῖ ἐν ἡμῖν, ἀλλ' ὁ ἐν τοῖς παρανόμοις οἰκῶν διάβολος. ᾧ γὰρ λέγω· Χριστὸς οἰκεῖ ἐν παντὶ δικαίῳ τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐργαζομένῳ, τὸν αὐτὸν οἶμαι τρόπον οἰκεῖν τὸν διάβολον ἐν παντὶ κακοποιῷ. οὐκοῦν οὐχ ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν καθὸ σάρκα ἔχομεν πονηροί, ἀλλ' ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἡμῖν ἁμαρτία, ἄλλη τις οὖσα παρὰ τὴν σάρκα καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου· καὶ γὰρ ἐν ψυχῇ μάλιστα λέγεται ἐπιχωριάζειν ὁ διάβολος κατὰ τὸ εἰσῆλθεν ὁ σατανᾶς εἰς τὴν καρδίαν Ἰούδα, καὶ κατὰ τὸ Ἀνανία, ἵνα τί ἐπλήρωσεν ὁ σατανᾶς τὴν καρδίαν σου; εὖ δὲ καὶ τὸ εἰπεῖν οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτὸ ἀλλ' ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία· ἔργου γὰρ καὶ κατέργου πολὺ τὸ μέσον, διότι τοῦ ἔργου προηγεῖται τὸ κάτεργον ὡς φέρε εἰπεῖν οἰκίας ἢ νηός· τὸ δὲ κάτεργον, τοῦτ' ἔστι τῆς ὕλης ἡ προπαρασκευή. ἡ τοίνυν οἰκοῦσα ἐν τοῖς ἁμαρτάνουσιν ἁμαρτία, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ὁ σατανᾶς, ὁμολογουμένως ἐν τοῖς λογισμοῖς ἡμῶν προκατεργάζεται τοῦ ἐσομένου κακοῦ τῆς ἰδέας, τὴν κατασκευήν, τῆς ὑποδεξαμένης αὐτὸν ψυχῆς συμπραττούσης αὐτῷ τῆς κακίας καθάπερ τοῖς σπείρουσιν ἡ τῆς θήλεος μήτρα πρὸς τὸ 3 τελεσφορηθῆναι τὸ σπαρέν. καὶ ἐπειδήπερ ἐκ τῆς καρδίας ἐκπορεύονται λογισμοὶ πονηροί, ἐκ τῆς γενομένης τοῦ διαβόλου συλλήψεως, κέκραγε τὸ θεῖον λόγιον· λογισμοὺς καθαιροῦντες καὶ πᾶν ὕψωμα ἐπαιρόμενον κατὰ τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ θεοῦ. ὥσπερ τοίνυν ταῖς φιλαρέτοις ψυχαῖς τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα συγκοπιᾶν λέγεται κατὰ τὸ περισσότερον πάντων ἐκοπίασα, οὐκ ἐγὼ δὲ ἀλλ' ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ σὺν ἐμοί, οὕτω δὴ ἐπὰν ῥᾴθυμος ψυχὴ ταῖς 6 τοῦ διαβόλου προτροπαῖς πεισθῇ, συνεργὸν ἔχει πρὸς τὸ κακὸν αὐτὸν τὸν διάβολον· αὐτὸς γὰρ καὶ τὸν τύπον τῆς ἐσομένης ἁμαρτίας προκατειργάσατο ἐν αὐτῇ. ὅτου χάριν εἴρηται οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτό, ἀλλ' ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία. 4
thought_title: The impious objection and the indwelling devil
orientation: Didymus is answering an impious objection to Paul's words in Romans 7, arguing that the flesh is not evil by nature but that the devil dwelling in evildoers works out sin.
pass_a_gloss: But if this is true, I will speak according to the impious: then the good was not nor will be in life, nor did anyone ever work it, if indeed they take it as the abolition of the good and the beautiful for every human, that 'the good I will, this I do not do, but what I hate, this I practice.' And from where were names of virtues found in the life of humans? But if there are those working the good, even if few are those doing this, will not all say: 'But we know that good does not dwell in us; for the good they willed, this they practice.' But if those working the good while being in flesh work this, and those not doing this but the evil are in flesh, then is not the cause of the good not coming to be to be attached to the flesh, but to the softness of soul of these? For if to those willing to do the good the evil dwells nearby, and likewise to those willing to do evil the good lies nearby, and having purposed beforehand and willed beforehand they come to such an extent of activity, then are not our bodies evil by nature and substance? For of our deeds, counsel and will go first, and these are the thought of a soul having free will, able to incline toward whatever actions it wishes. 'But now no longer am I working it out, but the sin dwelling in me.' He defended through this saying that the flesh is not evil by nature; for it is not the flesh which we wear that dwells in us, but the devil dwelling in the lawless. For in the way I say: Christ dwells in every righteous person working the good, in the same way I think the devil dwells in every evildoer. Therefore we are not evil insofar as we have flesh, but the sin dwelling in us, being something other than the flesh and the soul of the human; for indeed the devil is said to dwell especially in the soul, according to 'Satan entered into the heart of Judas,' and according to 'Ananias, why did Satan fill your heart?' And well is the saying 'no longer am I working it out, but the sin dwelling in me'; for between work and working-out there is much middle ground, because the working-out precedes the work, as for example of a house or a ship; and the working-out, that is, the prior preparation of the material. The sin therefore dwelling in those who sin, that is, Satan, admittedly works out beforehand in our reasonings the preparation of the idea of the coming evil, the soul that received him cooperating with him in the evil, just as with those sowing the womb of the female cooperates for the sown seed to be brought to completion. And since from the heart come forth evil reasonings, from the conception of the devil that has occurred, the divine saying cries out: 'destroying reasonings and every high thing lifted up against the knowledge of God.' Just as therefore the Holy Spirit is said to labor together with virtue-loving souls, according to 'I labored more abundantly than all, not I but the grace of God with me,' so indeed whenever a careless soul is persuaded by the promptings of the devil, it has the devil himself as a coworker toward evil; for he himself also worked out beforehand in it the pattern of the coming sin. For which reason it is said 'no longer am I working it out, but the sin dwelling in me.'

pass_b_english: But if this is true, I will speak according to the impious: then the good was not and will not be in life, nor did anyone ever work it, if they take the words “the good I will, this I do not do, but what I hate, this I practice” as the abolition of the good and noble in every human being. And from where were the names of virtues found in human life? But if there are those who work the good, even if those who do this are few, will not all make this claim: “We know that good does not dwell in us”? For the good they will, this they practice. But if those who work the good do so while existing in flesh, and those who do not do this but do evil are also in flesh, then the cause of the good not coming to be must not be attached to the flesh, but to the softness of soul of these people. For if evil dwells alongside for those who will to do the good, and likewise no good lies nearby for those who will to do evil, and having deliberated beforehand and willed beforehand they come to such a degree of activity, then our bodies are not evil by nature and substance. For deliberation and willing precede our actions, and these belong to a soul that has free will, able to incline toward whatever actions it wishes.

“But now it is no longer I who work it out, but the sin dwelling in me” (Romans 7:17). Through this saying he has defended the point that the flesh is not evil by nature. For it is not the flesh we are clothed with that dwells in us, but the devil who dwells in the lawless. For in the same way that I say Christ dwells in every righteous person who works the good, in the same way I think the devil dwells in every evildoer. Therefore we are not evil insofar as we have flesh, but the sin dwelling in us is something other than the flesh and the soul of the human being. For the devil is said to sojourn especially in the soul, according to “Satan entered into the heart of Judas” (John 13:27), and according to “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart?” (Acts 5:3). And it is well said, “no longer I work it out, but the sin dwelling in me.” For there is a great distance between a work and a working out, because the working out precedes the work, as for example of a house or a ship; the working out is the preliminary preparation of the material. So the sin dwelling in those who sin—that is, Satan—admittedly works out beforehand in our reasonings the pattern of the coming evil, the preparation, while the soul that has received him cooperates with him in the evil, just as the womb of the female cooperates with those who sow for the sown seed to come to term. And since evil reasonings come out of the heart, from the conception of the devil that has occurred, the divine saying cries out: “destroying reasonings and every high thing lifted up against the knowledge of God” (2 Corinthians 10:5). Just as the Holy Spirit is said to labor together with virtue-loving souls, according to “I labored more abundantly than all, yet not I but the grace of God with me” (1 Corinthians 15:10), so when a careless soul is persuaded by the devil’s urgings, it has the devil himself as a coworker toward evil. For he himself has worked out beforehand in it the pattern of the coming sin. For this reason it is said, “no longer I work it out, but the sin dwelling in me.”

problems.why: ἀγαθοῦ means 'good,' not 'beautiful'; 'good and beautiful' misrepresents the paired terms.
problems.fix: the good and the good, or simply 'the good'

problems.quote: will not all say, "We know that good does not dwell in us"?
problems.source_quote: ἄρ' οὐχ οἱ πάντες φήσουσιν· οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι οὐκ οἰκεῖ ἐν ἡμῖν ἀγαθόν
problems.why: Source says 'will not all confess [the opposite]?' then quotes 'we know good does not dwell in us'; English merges them, losing the rhetorical counter-confession.
problems.fix: will not all confess the opposite? For we know that good does not dwell in us.
problems.ruling: Greek has two distinct clauses: rhetorical question (ἄρ' οὐχ οἱ πάντες φήσουσιν) then quotation (οἴδαμεν δὲ...). English merges into one, losing the rhetorical structure and making Pauline quote appear as universal consensus rather than contested confession.

problems.why: οὐ καλὸν means 'not good'/'evil,' not 'the good'; the phrase says evil lies close by for those willing to do evil, not good.
problems.ruling: οὐ καλὸν = 'not good' (i.e., evil), not 'the good'; translation reverses meaning.

problems.source_quote: ἐκ τῆς καρδίας ἐκπορεύονται λογισμοὶ πονηροί
problems.why: The quoted words 'evil reasonings come out of the heart' do not match Matthew 15:19, which has 'ἐκ γὰρ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχονται διαλογισμοὶ πονηροί' (evil thoughts come out); the allusion is closer to Mark 7:21 or a conflation, but cited as Matthew 15:19 with altered wording.
problems.ruling: Source has λογισμοὶ not διαλογισμοὶ; Matthew 15:19 wording differs, citation may mislead readers.

edits.old: will not all say, "We know that good does not dwell in us"? For the good they willed, this they practice.
edits.new: will not all confess the opposite? For we know that good does not dwell in us; for the good they willed, this they practice.

edits.new: evil lies close by for those who will to do evil

fixed: Corrected 'the good and beautiful' to 'the good and the good' per source 'τοῦ καλοῦ καὶ ἀγαθοῦ' (both terms mean 'good').

Corrected the rhetorical question to preserve the counter-confession: source 'ἄρ' οὐχ οἱ πάντες φήσουσιν· οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι οὐκ οἰκεῖ ἐν ἡμῖν ἀγαθόν' means 'will not all confess [the opposite]? For we know that good does not dwell in us.'
Corrected 'the good lies close by' to 'evil lies close by' per source 'οὐ καλὸν παράκειται' (not good/evil lies close by).
Changed scripture citation from Matthew 15:19 to Mark 7:21, as the quoted words 'evil reasonings come out of the heart' match Mark 7:21 more closely than Matthew 15:19.

problems.quote: evil lies close by for those who will to do evil
problems.source_quote: τοῖς ἐθέλουσι κακοεργεῖν οὐ καλὸν παράκειται
problems.why: Source says "good lies nearby" (οὐ καλὸν παράκειται = good does not lie nearby, i.e., no good is at hand), not "evil lies close by."
problems.fix: no good lies nearby for those who will to do evil

problems.quote: the preparation of the pattern of the coming evil
problems.source_quote: τοῦ ἐσομένου κακοῦ τῆς ἰδέας, τὴν κατασκευήν
problems.why: Word order garbled: "the pattern of the coming evil, the preparation"—τῆς ἰδέας goes with τοῦ ἐσομένου κακοῦ (pattern of the coming evil), then τὴν κατασκευήν (the preparation) is separate object.
problems.fix: the pattern of the coming evil, the preparation

problems.quote: will not all say, "We know that good does not dwell in us"?
problems.source_quote: ἄρ' οὐχ οἱ πάντες φήσουσιν· οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι οὐκ οἰκεῖ ἐν ἡμῖν ἀγαθόν
problems.why: Paul's words 'we know that good does not dwell in us' are presented as the impious conclusion, not as a quotation the impious themselves speak.
problems.fix: will not all make this claim: 'We know that good does not dwell in us'?
problems.ruling: ἄρ' οὐχ οἱ πάντες φήσουσιν introduces a question expecting 'yes'—the impious will say this; οἴδαμεν δὲ is their quotation, not Paul's. English wrongly makes 'We know' a separate assertion by 'all,' misattributing the voice and breaking the rhetorical structure.

problems.quote: as the abolition of the good and the good on every human being
problems.source_quote: κατ' ἀναίρεσιν τοῦ καλοῦ καὶ ἀγαθοῦ ἐπὶ παντὸς ἀνθρώπου ἐκλαμβάνωσιν
problems.why: "the good and the good" is gibberish; source has "the good and the noble/good" (καλοῦ καὶ ἀγαθοῦ) as paired terms, not repeated.
problems.fix: as the abolition of the good and noble in every human being
problems.ruling: καλοῦ καὶ ἀγαθοῦ are distinct paired terms ('beautiful' and 'good'), not 'the good and the good'—gibberish that obscures meaning

problems.quote: evil reasonings come out of the heart (Mark 7:21)
problems.source_quote: ἐκ τῆς καρδίας ἐκπορεύονται λογισμοὶ πονηροί
problems.why: The citation Mark 7:21 is wrong; this alludes to Matthew 15:19/Mark 7:21 but the exact phrase here is not quoted as Scripture—Didymus uses it as premise, then quotes 2 Cor 10:5. More importantly, the Greek has no citation here; the English adds one misleadingly.
problems.fix: evil reasonings come out of the heart
problems.ruling: Source has no Scripture citation; English inserts '(Mark 7:21)' misleadingly, implying a formal quote where Didymus uses the phrase as premise

problems.quote: the evil I hate, this I practice
problems.source_quote: ὃ θέλω ἀγαθόν, τοῦτο οὐ ποιῶ, ἀλλ' ὃ μισῶ τοῦτο πράσσω
problems.why: Source says 'the good I will, this I do not do, but what I hate, this I practice'—English inverts to 'evil I hate', misquoting Romans 7:19.
problems.fix: the good I will, this I do not do, but what I hate, this I practice

problems.why: παροικεῖται means 'dwells alongside/paradwells', not merely 'nearby'; the devil's indwelling is stronger.

problems.quote: the pattern of the coming evil, the preparation

problems.why: τῆς ἰδέας is genitive with τοῦ ἐσομένου κακοῦ: 'the pattern/idea of the coming evil, the preparation'.
problems.fix: the pattern of the coming evil, the preparation

problems.quote: the good they willed, this they practice
problems.source_quote: ὃ γὰρ ἠθέλησαν ἀγαθόν, τοῦτο πράττουσιν
problems.why: Context is about those who work good; 'they willed' should be 'they will' (present), matching 'they practice.'
problems.fix: for the good they will, this they practice
problems.ruling: ἠθέλησαν is aorist 'willed,' but context requires present 'will' to match πράττουσιν and parallel ἐθέλουσιν.

problems.quote: is said to be at home especially in the soul
problems.source_quote: ἐν ψυχῇ μάλιστα λέγεται ἐπιχωριάζειν ὁ διάβολος
problems.why: ἐπιχωριάζειν means 'sojourn/dwell temporarily', not 'be at home'; it contrasts with οἰκεῖν.
problems.fix: is said to sojourn especially in the soul
problems.ruling: ἐπιχωριάζειν means sojourn/dwell temporarily; 'at home' reverses the contrast with οἰκεῖν.

fixed: Changed 'the evil I hate, this I practice' to 'what I hate, this I practice' to match source 'ὃ μισῶ τοῦτο πράσσω'.
Changed 'evil dwells nearby' to 'evil dwells alongside' to reflect παροικεῖται as dwelling alongside.
Changed 'the good they willed, this they practice' to 'the good they will, this they practice' to match present tense ἠθέλησαν in context.
Changed 'is said to be at home especially in the soul' to 'is said to sojourn especially in the soul' to reflect ἐπιχωριάζειν as sojourning, not being at home.

dismissed.quote: will not all make this claim
dismissed.why: Greek asks a rhetorical question expecting 'yes'; English turns it into a negative statement.
dismissed.note: The English is already a rhetorical question ending in '?', so it does not turn the Greek into a statement.

dismissed.quote: For the good they will, this they practice
dismissed.why: English uses future 'will' but Greek has aorist 'willed/wished'; this obscures Didymus's argument about actual doers of good.
dismissed.note: 'Will' here is the verb 'to will', not a future tense; tense nuance aside, the meaning is kept.
